title: Darwin on divergence
statement: Natural selection, as has just been remarked, leads to divergence of character and to much extinction of the less improved and intermediate forms of life.
cite: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species, 1859, chapter IV, Natural Selection (Project Gutenberg ebook 1228, public domain).
question: A parent species throws off varieties, and the better-suited ones are kept, generation after generation. Which descendants does natural selection tend to preserve?
options: The most different from each other
